input: Given /data/team_a.txt and /data/team_b.txt containing member names (one per line, already sorted), use the comm command to find: 1) Members only in Team A (print under 'Only Team A:'). 2) Members only in Team B (print under 'Only Team B:'). 3) Members in both teams (print under 'Both teams:'). Print the count of each group.

tool_calls:
comm -23 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt > /tmp/only_a
comm -13 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt > /tmp/only_b
comm -12 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt > /tmp/both
printf 'Only Team A:\n'
cat /tmp/only_a
printf 'Count: '; wc -l < /tmp/only_a
printf 'Only Team B:\n'
cat /tmp/only_b
printf 'Count: '; wc -l < /tmp/only_b
printf 'Both teams:\n'
cat /tmp/both
printf 'Count: '; wc -l < /tmp/both
